meta.title: RAG Evaluation Metrics
meta.thesis: RAG Evaluation Metrics is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A docs-search assistant returns confident answers and the team needs metrics that separate retrieval from generation. By the end, they should be able to build or review RAG metric rubric for context recall, precision, faithfulness, and answer relevance, measure faithfulness and context recall by question type, and catch the failure where a single accuracy score hides whether retrieval or generation failed.

mentalMap.title: RAG Evaluation Metrics: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Separate RAG evaluation into retrieval arrival, context usefulness, answer faithfulness, citation support, and slice-level decisions.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: RAG metrics are useful when they diagnose which part failed: evidence retrieval, context selection, answer generation, or citation support.

modules.title: Retrieval metrics ask whether evidence arrived
modules.sub: Before judging answers, check the top-k context.
modules.summary: Hit rate, recall@k, MRR, and nDCG diagnose the search layer.
objectives: Explain retrieval metrics with a concrete docs-assistant case.
Distinguish source-based evaluation from answer evaluation.
Use negative cases where no evidence should be retrieved.

blocks.title: If evidence is absent, the generator is guessing

spans.text: Problem anchor: a docs assistant answers a refund-policy question with a confident but wrong paragraph. The model might be hallucinating, or the retriever might have missed the policy page. Retrieval metrics answer the first question: did the needed evidence arrive in the context window?
Use hit rate or recall@k when each query has expected source IDs. Use MRR or nDCG when rank matters. A source found at rank 20 is not useful if the prompt only includes top 5.

blocks.analogy: Retrieval metrics check whether the ingredients reached the counter before judging the meal.

blocks.title: Worked retrieval row: refund cutoff question

spans.text: Query: "Can I get a refund after 45 days?" Expected source: refunds.md#45. Retriever returns top five: shipping.md#12, cancellation.md#7, refunds.md#45, pricing.md#2, support.md#9. hit@5 is true, reciprocal rank is 1/3, and hit@2 is false. The answer may still fail later, but the retrieval diagnosis is specific.

blocks.title: Retrieval first

options.text: Because retrieval metrics prove the answer is well written.
Because an answer cannot be grounded in evidence that never arrived.
Because top-k ranking never changes.

blocks.explanation: Separate retrieval diagnosis from generation diagnosis.

modules.title: Context precision asks how much retrieved text helps
modules.sub: High recall can still drown the prompt in distracting chunks.
modules.summary: Context precision catches noisy retrieval that crowds out useful evidence.
objectives: Explain precision versus recall in RAG context.
Identify chunking and reranking failures from noisy context.
Choose a top-k that matches the prompt budget.

blocks.title: Recall finds the needle; precision removes hay

spans.text: A retriever can include the right refund chunk and still fail the user by surrounding it with irrelevant shipping, pricing, and cancellation chunks. Context precision asks how much of the supplied context actually helps answer the question.

In practice, this points to chunk boundaries, metadata filters, hybrid weighting, and reranking. If context recall is high but precision is low, do not immediately change the model prompt. Inspect what the retriever packed into the prompt.

blocks.title: Two rankings with the same hit rate

spans.text: Ranking A puts refunds.md#45 first, followed by related cancellation policy. Ranking B puts refunds.md#45 fifth after four generic support chunks. Both have hit@5=true, but Ranking A is more likely to produce a faithful answer within a limited prompt budget.

modules.title: Faithfulness and answer relevance judge generation
modules.sub: Once evidence is present, check whether the answer uses it correctly.
modules.summary: Answer metrics evaluate grounded synthesis, not retrieval alone.
objectives: Define faithfulness and answer relevance in RAG.
Avoid mixing retrieval misses with generation failures.
Use judge metrics with spot checks and versioned rubrics.

blocks.title: Faithfulness is about support; relevance is about answering the question

spans.text: Ragas-style metrics include signals such as faithfulness, context precision, context recall, and response relevancy. Faithfulness asks whether the answer claims are supported by retrieved context. Answer relevance asks whether the answer addresses the user question instead of merely repeating context.

Keep the stage boundary clear. If the right source is absent, faithfulness may punish the answer, but the actionable fix begins in retrieval. If the source is present and the answer invents a refund exception, the fix is prompting, output constraints, or model behavior.

The assistant says: "Refunds are automatic only within 30 days." That is faithful to the context, but it does not answer whether a 45-day customer can escalate. A relevance check or task-completion rubric should catch the missing escalation guidance.

modules.title: Citation quality ties claims to specific sources
modules.sub: Users need to inspect support, not just receive a confidence score.
modules.summary: Citation checks make RAG answers auditable claim by claim.
objectives: Compute simple retrieval and citation-support metrics.
Predict how missing citations affect the report.
Verify AI-generated RAG eval code for source alignment.

blocks.title: Tiny RAG eval report for source and citation support
blocks.code:
cases = [
    {
        "id": "refund_45_days",
        "expected_sources": {"refunds.md#45"},
        "retrieved": ["shipping.md#12", "refunds.md#45", "support.md#9"],
        "answer_citations": {"refunds.md#45"},
        "claims_supported": 3,
        "claims_total": 3,
    },
    {
        "id": "enterprise_sla",
        "expected_sources": {"enterprise-sla.md#2"},
        "retrieved": ["pricing.md#1", "support.md#9"],
        "answer_citations": set(),
        "claims_supported": 1,
        "claims_total": 3,
    },
]

for case in cases:
    retrieved = set(case["retrieved"])
    recall_at_3 = bool(case["expected_sources"] & retrieved)
    citation_support = case["expected_sources"] <= case["answer_citations"]
    faithfulness = case["claims_supported"] / case["claims_total"]
    print(case["id"], {
        "recall_at_3": recall_at_3,
        "citation_support": citation_support,
        "faithfulness": round(faithfulness, 2),
    })

spans.text: This is intentionally small. It separates retrieval success, citation support, and claim support so the fix is diagnosable.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Predict the report for enterprise_sla. Which metric points to retrieval failure?
predictThenReveal.answer: enterprise_sla has recall_at_3 false because enterprise-sla.md#2 is absent from retrieved sources. citation_support is also false, and faithfulness is 0.33, but retrieval is the first failure to investigate.

spans.text: Checklist: expected sources are explicit; retrieved source IDs come from the real retriever; top-k matches production prompt packing; answer citations are compared to source IDs, not titles; negative cases expect no sufficient evidence; and aggregate scores can be broken down by slice.

modules.title: Slice dashboards prevent aggregate deception
modules.sub: Averages hide the queries that hurt users most.
modules.summary: RAG evals become release gates when metrics are sliced by task, source, and risk.
objectives: Explain why aggregate RAG metrics can mislead.
Define slices for docs, policy, freshness, and no-answer cases.
Set thresholds that route fixes to retrieval or generation owners.

blocks.title: A passing average can hide a dangerous slice

spans.text: A docs assistant can score 0.89 overall while failing every policy question updated last week. Slice by topic, source type, freshness, language, user intent, and negative no-evidence cases. Track retrieval metrics and answer metrics separately in each slice.

items.text: Policy slice: stricter citation and refusal threshold.
Freshness slice: expected source must match current version.
No-evidence slice: correct answer is insufficient evidence.
Long-tail slice: inspect manually before trusting aggregate scores.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Use RAG metrics as diagnostics, not a single trophy score.
blocks.useWhen: Use them before changing embeddings, chunking, rerankers, prompt packing, or model settings, and whenever an index is rebuilt.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid optimizing one aggregate score while ignoring no-answer cases, stale ground truth, judge variance, or category regressions.

blocks.title: Metric decision
blocks.prompt: A RAG system has high overall faithfulness but fails no-evidence questions. What should the team do?

options.text: Declare the release safe because the average is high.
Add a no-evidence slice with refusal/citation thresholds and inspect retrieval behavior.
Only rewrite the UI copy.

blocks.explanation: Slices reveal failures that averages can hide.

eval.label: Eval
eval.laymanDefinition: A repeatable test of model or system behavior against expected criteria.
eval.technicalNote: In these lessons, evals are release evidence: they combine cases, assertions, scores, and review rules.

trace.label: Trace
trace.laymanDefinition: A structured record of one run, including spans, inputs, outputs, metadata, and scores.
trace.technicalNote: Traces make failures diagnosable by showing which retrieval, model, tool, or scoring step produced the result.

dataset.label: Dataset
dataset.laymanDefinition: A curated set of examples used for evaluation, debugging, or regression checks.
dataset.technicalNote: A useful eval dataset stores inputs, expected behavior, metadata slices, and source or rubric references.

judge.label: LLM-as-judge
judge.laymanDefinition: An LLM used to grade or compare outputs with a rubric.
judge.technicalNote: LLM judges are semantic scorers, not final authority; their prompts, model, thresholds, and spot checks must be versioned.

regression.label: Regression
regression.laymanDefinition: A previously working behavior that breaks after a prompt, model, data, or code change.
regression.technicalNote: Regression testing protects known capabilities and safety boundaries while allowing harmless wording variation.

rubric.label: Rubric
rubric.laymanDefinition: A scoring guide that states what a good answer or run must demonstrate.
rubric.technicalNote: Rubrics make qualitative judgment reviewable by naming criteria, severity, examples, and thresholds.

finalCheck.title: Knowledge check
finalCheck.intro: A quick check across the whole lesson — pick or type your answers.

questions.prompt: A docs assistant is tested on a question whose answer does not exist in any indexed document. Which retrieval outcome is correct?

options.text: The system should retrieve the closest partial match and flag low confidence.
No chunks should be retrieved, because a true negative is the right result here.
Recall should be maximized by retrieving all available chunks.
Faithfulness is the only metric that matters when no answer exists.

questions.explanation: When no relevant evidence exists, the correct retrieval behavior is to return nothing — retrieving irrelevant chunks would inflate noise and mislead generation.

questions.prompt: Your RAG pipeline retrieves 8 chunks for every query, but only 2 are ever cited or used by the generator. Which problem does this most directly indicate?

options.text: Low faithfulness — the model is hallucinating answers.
Low context precision — too many irrelevant chunks are crowding the prompt.
Low answer relevance — the response does not address the question.
A citation-quality failure — sources are not being linked to claims.

questions.explanation: Context precision measures how much of the retrieved text is actually useful; retrieving many chunks while only a few contribute signals a noisy retrieval or reranking failure.

questions.prompt: An LLM-as-judge scores a generated answer as highly faithful, but a spot check reveals the answer contradicts one of the retrieved chunks. What is the most likely root cause of this discrepancy?

options.text: The retrieval recall was too low, so the right chunk was never fetched.
The judge rubric was not versioned, so it drifted from the intended faithfulness definition.
Context precision was too high, leaving no room for the correct chunk.
The citation-support metric was not computed alongside faithfulness.

questions.explanation: Without versioned rubrics and regular spot checks, judge prompts drift — the judge may reward fluency or confidence rather than strict grounding in the retrieved context.

questions.prompt: In a RAG system that generates a financial report, explain in 1–2 sentences why missing citations on specific claims are a problem — and which metric you would use to catch this.
questions.acceptableAnswer: Missing citations mean readers cannot verify which source supports a claim, making the report untrustworthy and potentially wrong without anyone noticing. Citation-support rate (the share of claims that link back to a specific retrieved source) is the metric used to catch this.
questions.explanation: Citation quality ties each generated claim to a retrievable source; without it, errors in generation are invisible and the report cannot be audited.

questions.prompt: A RAG system shows 85% faithfulness overall, but policy-related queries score only 52%. What is the correct action, and why do aggregate metrics hide this?

options.text: Retrain the retriever on all query types equally, because aggregate metrics are already reliable.
Raise the top-k for all queries to improve recall across the board.
Create a policy slice dashboard and route the fix to the team responsible for generation on policy content, since the aggregate masks the slice-level failure.
Lower the faithfulness threshold so the policy slice passes, balancing the overall score.

questions.explanation: Aggregate metrics average over all slices and can hide severe failures in specific categories; slice dashboards expose these gaps and route fixes to the right owner — retrieval or generation.
